scenes.text: This tiny shrimp punches so fast that the water around its fist starts to boil.
The mantis shrimp swings its club at about fifty miles per hour, in less than three thousandths of a second.
That's an acceleration of up to ten thousand times the force of gravity.
The strike is so fast it creates bubbles that collapse with a second hit, and even tiny flashes of light.
It uses this punch to smash open crabs and snail shells.
One mantis shrimp at an aquarium even broke through a glass wall.
Would you keep one as a pet?

title: This shrimp punches so fast the water boils 🦐
caption: The mantis shrimp's club hits at about 50 mph with up to 10,000 g of acceleration. The strike makes collapsing cavitation bubbles that hit a second time and even flash with light. 🦐
